candidates.summary: China's coast guard conducted patrols east of Taiwan that Beijing described as routine law enforcement. Taiwan's coast guard said two Chinese ships were involved, accused them of harassing shipping by radio and sent its own vessels to monitor. Taiwan also reported a separate Chinese coast guard ship near the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands. Taiwan rejects Beijing's sovereignty and jurisdiction claims.
candidates.title: Taiwan deploys ships in response to Chinese coast guard patrols
candidates.geography: Taiwan Strait and waters east of Taiwan

candidates.summary: Tens of thousands of people demonstrated in 34 German cities for greater investment in education, lower living costs and opposition to compulsory military service. Authorities said the demonstrations were largely peaceful, but hooded rioters looted at least two stores and damaged others in Frankfurt. Police reported Molotov cocktails thrown at emergency services, while barricades were burned in Hamburg.
candidates.title: German youth-led protests turn violent in Frankfurt

candidates.summary: The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 to win the WNBA championship in the franchise's second season. Gabby Williams scored 30 points, including Golden State's final 11 points of the third quarter, and received the Finals MVP award. It was the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history.
candidates.title: Golden State Valkyries win WNBA championship

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump said defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro could remain in the United States for as long as he wanted, while saying he had no plans to meet him. Reuters reported that Bolsonaro entered under humanitarian parole, a status that typically lasts one year. Brazil had revoked Bolsonaro's passport amid money-laundering investigations and concerns that he might flee.
candidates.title: Trump says Flávio Bolsonaro can remain in U.S.

candidates.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to considering a formal state apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade. He ruled out financial reparations but proposed structured dialogue with affected countries and assistance including improved debt terms. Caribbean leaders were expected to raise reparatory-justice demands at the following week's Commonwealth summit.
candidates.title: UK prime minister open to slavery apology but rejects reparations

candidates.summary: Court documents obtained by the Associated Press disclosed that the Trump administration was preparing to deport detained Afghan immigrants through Pakistan for onward transport to Afghanistan. A senior immigration official acknowledged the planned routing in a filing made Friday. The Department of Homeland Security declined Saturday to comment on future removal operations, and it was unclear whether affected people had legal protections barring their return.
candidates.title: Court filings disclose U.S. plan to deport Afghans through Pakistan

candidates.summary: The FBI contacted donors to Alaska Senate candidate Dan J. Sullivan as federal authorities expanded an investigation into whether his candidacy was intended to confuse voters because he shares the Republican incumbent's name. Donors interviewed by the Associated Press said they knowingly supported the retired teacher and did not feel deceived. Democratic challenger Mary Peltola and Sullivan denied coordinating his candidacy.
candidates.title: FBI contacts donors as Alaska Senate inquiry expands

candidates.summary: Relatives of people detained or disappeared under El Salvador's state of exception gathered at San Salvador's metropolitan cathedral to honor people who died in custody and demand fair trials. Participants carried photographs and left flowers at Archbishop Óscar Romero's tomb. Human-rights organization Cristosal said it had documented 454 prison deaths among people detained under the emergency policy.
candidates.title: Salvadoran families demand fair trials for emergency detainees
